title: Constructibility and Tor under the first integral quotient comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite field extension E of Q_l and a Noetherian scheme X. Let A be the lifted valuation ring of E, I its lifted uniformizer ideal [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients], k=A/I, and assume its Noetherian-ring instance explicitly (it holds since k is a field). For any internal complex K over the continuous integral coefficients, let F(K) be its canonical integral realization [def-sfb-integral-constant-model-realization] and M the fixedScalarDerivedModel of its literal sfbResidueComplex [def-sfb-fixed-scalar-complex-model, def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. Then residueCondition for the constant scalar restriction of K [def-sfb-integral-models-stacks-data] is equivalent to affine-locally constructible cohomology of M [def-sfb-affine-locally-constructible-proetale-modules] and finite global coefficient-model Tor amplitude [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. No completeness or etale-origin hypothesis or conclusion enters this coefficient comparison.

source.place: Proof (1)--(2), common-quotient residue comparison; proetale.tex Tags 099C, 099M and 09C1

proof.text: Instantiate the normalized discrete coefficient model for A=O_E/(pi_E), k=ULift(O_E)/(ULift(pi_E)) and the reverse of integralCoefficientULift at index zero. Its constructed functor F is an additive monoidal equivalence and transports finite-constant-model constructibility on module sheaves. The normalized common-quotient comparison gives an isomorphism i from D(F) of the Stacks first residue to the fixed-scalar first residue M.

Apply the exact functor cohomology isomorphism to each degree and then homology to i. Transport constructibility along that isomorphism and the heart-level equivalence. This proves the first conjunct in both directions.

A monoidal equivalence preserves flat objects. The proved exact faithful monoidal derived Tor comparison transports native finite Tor amplitude through F, and isomorphism invariance transports it through i. Apply nativeTor_iff from the coefficient flat-model module to identify the native predicate with the coefficient-model predicate. For an unordered native interval [a,b], widen its lower bound to min(a,b); the coefficient predicate supplies ordered endpoints in the reverse direction. Combine these independent equivalences with and_congr.

proof_origin.place: Z9 stage-3 reduction: explicit exact-derived homology and native Tor transport from a normalized heart equivalence and a common-residue isomorphism; the unit route in integral-models (1)--(2) is preserved.

theorem integral_residue_coefficient_transport (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X]
    (hk : IsNoetherianRing
      (IntegralConstantCompletion.integers l E ⧸ IntegralConstantCompletion.ideal l E ^ (0 + 1)))
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (integersObj l E) X))) :
    letI := hk
    let k := IntegralConstantCompletion.integers l E ⧸
      IntegralConstantCompletion.ideal l E ^ (0 + 1)
    let M := Scheme.fixedScalarDerivedModel X k
      (Scheme.sfbResidueComplex X (IntegralConstantCompletion.ideal l E)
        ((IntegralConstantModel.derived l E X).functor.obj K))
    residueCondition l E X ((restriction l E X).obj K) ↔
      (∀ q : ℤ, Scheme.IsCoefficientAffineLocallyConstructibleProEtaleModuleSheaf.{u, u} X k
        ((coefficientModelCohomology _ q).obj M)) ∧
      Scheme.HasFiniteCoefficientProEtaleTorAmplitude.{u, u} X k M
